scenes.title: 01 · ONE BALL. EIGHT VOICES.
scenes.body: August. A basketball meets a kick drum. Isaiah “Zay” Reed, twenty-six and 6'8", plays with joy. Seven artists join his rhythm in separate colors. Before triumph, silence: a cramped Las Vegas kitchen. His mother demands money and humiliates his dream. He leaves with a ball and a small bag.

scenes.title: 02 · THE MEN CALLED UNCLE
scenes.body: Denise, a cabaret server, struggles with alcohol addiction. Her boyfriends were always “Uncle.” Ray kept coaching Zay after divorcing her. At eighteen, Zay’s absent biological father died as college basketball became possible; afterward, Zay discovered his father’s submitted grant applications. Grieving, with Denise and Ray divorced, he declined college and available aid to support his family. Eight years of work, training, and saving buy a flight toward his Knicks dream. Ray drives him to the airport.

scenes.title: 03 · AFTER THE APPLAUSE
scenes.body: The next evening, childhood friend Dani Price is doing comedy at New York’s The Switch. Zay meets Lena Marlow, a ballet-trained exotic dancer. Teasing becomes an intimate duet. Then he says she could be a “real dancer again.” She orders him out. Humiliated at home, he has now dismissed someone else’s livelihood.

scenes.title: 04 · THE PEOPLE WHO MAKE ROOM
scenes.body: Dani and actor roommate Ben Mercer negotiate a place for Zay. Ben’s gallery work connects painter Iris Chen to a court-side mural; she paints Zay without his invincible pose. Lena and composer Morgan Ellis create a movement piece. Andre Bell, as Velvet Saint, hires lead guitarist Jude Reyes for a headline act. Rent, rehearsal, attraction, and favors bring their ambitions together.

scenes.title: 05 · TALENT IS ONLY THE BEGINNING
scenes.body: Ray introduces Coach Simone Vale, who prepares Zay for a September Westchester Knicks G League tryout. No camp invitation follows. He must improve his defense, passing, conditioning, and response to correction. Next: November 15, game film for the fictional, independent Lake Erie Forge. Meanwhile, Dani’s joke exposes Ben’s private history, and Morgan and Jude avoid discussing credit.

scenes.title: 06 · EVERYONE IN HIS FRAME
scenes.body: A sponsor offers camp travel for an inspirational film. Zay approves Rise of Reed, turning private footage, Iris’s unfinished portrait, and his friends’ disclosures into evidence of his ascent. Morgan licenses their cue without permission. The film gets attention. The people inside it recognize the betrayal. Act I leaves Zay on a screen and alone beneath it.

scenes.title: 07 · WHAT REPAIR COSTS
scenes.body: Zay withdraws the film, corrects the record, and loses the sponsor. Extra shifts replace publicity. Morgan returns the fee and negotiates credits with Jude. Dani apologizes without a punchline and rewrites the audition. Iris insists on permission; Ben asks for clear terms. Velvet rejects a lucrative caricature booking. After Zay’s specific apology, Lena eventually offers him a limited role in her piece.

scenes.title: 08 · TWO PROMISES. ONE DATE.
scenes.body: December. Zay earns a Forge callback in Buffalo for December 14—the date of Lena and Morgan’s New York premiere. He tells them, transfers his fee to a rehearsed substitute, and pays for replacement labor. Ben keeps his acting call. Lena keeps her show. Zay stays at camp without making everyone else abandon their work.

scenes.title: 09 · THE EXTRA PASS
scenes.body: In Buffalo, Zay accepts correction and makes the extra pass. In New York, a lighting failure tests the company; Lena holds the count and Morgan finds the next entrance. The premiere succeeds; everyone stacks chairs. Progress arrives separately: Dani’s paid booking, Ben’s acting role, Iris’s commission, Velvet’s smaller headline run, and credited work for Morgan and Jude.

scenes.title: 10 · LEAVE SOME ROOM
scenes.body: Days later, Zay receives a six-week paid Forge contract. The Knicks remain a dream. Denise’s recovery remains her responsibility; Ray remains a mentor with limits. Lena begins another project and offers Zay coffee without promising romance. The opening rhythm returns. Zay listens between impacts. Every person can carry the pulse. Eight colors stay distinct; their lives remain unfinished.
